non_claims: The sulfate position on the ring is not resolved (regioisomers give near-identical spectra).
Aromatic versus vinyl (enol) attachment is not resolved.
The number of sulfate groups is not claimed; only mono-sulfate hypotheses are tried.

notes: Aromatic sulfates lose SO3 and give the SO3 radical anion (Lafaye 2004; Fitzgerald 2022), while an intense HSO4- points to alkyl or benzylic sulfation (Taglioni 2025), so HSO4- stronger than both vetoes the rule.

competitors.note: Alkyl, alicyclic and some benzylic sulfates give an intense HSO4- (Lafaye 2004; Taglioni 2025); benzyl sulfate, an isomer of p-cresyl sulfate, gives m/z 95.951 and no HSO4- (Correia 2020).
C-sulfonates also carry an SO3 group.
H2PO4- and the HPO3 loss sit 9.5 mDa from HSO4- and the SO3 loss; the p2 product tolerance and the observed-precursor loss reference keep them apart.

priors.note: Only mono-sulfate [M-H]- hypotheses are tried: bis-sulfates ionise mainly as [M-2H]2-, a charge state outside the v1 format.
